description: Large scaled multi-phase enclosure system that is thought to have operated in at least some religious capacity throughout its life. Earliest features are Middle - Late Iron Age enclosures, one of which surrounded a grave. Went through several phases before it's dismantling around 70 CE. This has occasionally been tied to either the Boudiccan revolt or some retribution immediately following it. Some evidence for re-use in the 3rd and 4th CE, as well as the Thetford treasure being found just to the south.
bibliography: Gregory, T. “Excavations in Thetford, 1980-1982, Fison Way.” East Anglian Archaeology 53 (1991).
Martyn, Blick, Brindle, and et al. “Fison Way, Thetford (Norfolk).” The Rural Settlement of Roman Britain: an online resource, 2015. https://doi.org/10.5284/1030449.
